title: Bisque de crevettes
subtitle: French prawn bisque
excerpt: Smooth, cream-enriched soup made from prawn shells roasted with aromatics, wine, and brandy. The more accessible sibling of bisque de homard: same technique, same rich result, using whole prawns with their shells.
sourceNotes: Bisque de crevettes follows the same classical technique as bisque de homard, documented in Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire (1903) and widely reproduced in French culinary reference works in the public domain. The method is identical; only the crustacean changes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the bisque base before adding cream. Defrost overnight in the fridge, reheat gently, add cream to finish.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Base can be made 2 days ahead. Add cream and reheat gently before serving.

content.text: Bisque de crevettes uses the same technique as the lobster version but starts from whole raw prawns. You peel them, keeping every shell, cook the shells with brandy and wine to make an intensely flavoured base, strain and reduce, then add cream. The peeled prawn meat goes back in at the very end. The result is deeply flavoured, silky, and achievable on a weeknight if you buy raw shell-on prawns.

items.prepNote: shell on, heads on if possible; peeled (shells reserved), deveined

content.text: Heat a splash of oil in a large saucepan over high heat until very hot. Add the prawn shells and heads and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until they turn pink and smell fragrant. They will colour and caramelise in places; this is what you want.

Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Add the tomato purée and stir in. Pour in the brandy, let it bubble and reduce. Add the wine and reduce by half. Pour in the fish stock and bring to the boil. Simmer for 30 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve into a clean pan, pressing hard on the shells. Discard the solids. Bring to the boil and reduce by one third.
Add the double cream and simmer for 5 minutes. Whisk in the butter. Season with salt and a pinch of cayenne.
Add the peeled prawn meat to the hot bisque and let them cook in the residual heat for 2 minutes until just firm. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Bisque lacks depth despite following the recipe
items.cause: Shells not cooked at high enough heat, or not enough reduction
items.fix: The shell-frying step needs high heat to caramelise the shells properly. Reduce the strained base further before adding cream.
Add the peeled prawn meat only at the end, off the heat or over very gentle heat. 2 minutes is enough.

content.text: Bisque de crevettes is the everyday version of the grand lobster bisque. It is found in coastal French restaurants and home kitchens throughout Brittany, Normandy, and the Atlantic coast, wherever shell-on prawns are easy to buy. The technique is identical to the lobster version; only the price and the prestige change. If you can buy raw prawns with their shells and heads, this bisque is worth making on an ordinary Tuesday.
